pages.title: Plan less. Do more. Feel calmer.
pages.content:
Why people switch

A planner that feels like a deep breath

Nestly keeps today short, the week visible and everything else out of the way.

☀️

Today, not someday

A short list for today, picked from everything else in seconds each morning.

⏳

Focus sessions

A gentle timer that silences notifications and logs what you finished.

🌱

Habits that stick

Tiny daily goals with a week view that forgives a missed day.

🔄

Sync everywhere

Phone, tablet and laptop stay in step, even offline.

Feature tour

Three screens, one calm day

Plan

See the week at a glance

Drag tasks between days, spot the overloaded Thursday and move things before it happens. Calendar events appear alongside, read-only.

  • Drag and drop between days
  • Calendar events alongside tasks
  • Gentle warnings for overloaded days

Focus

Do one thing at a time

Start a session from any task. Nestly silences notifications, keeps the screen calm and asks what you finished when the timer ends.

Grow

Habits without the guilt

Track up to ten small habits with a dot for each day. Missed one? The week view shows progress, not broken streaks.

Reviews

Small app, big difference

The first planner I have kept using past the second week. The Today list is short on purpose and that is the magic.

Reviewer on the app store

Focus sessions replaced three separate timer apps. The end-of-session question is oddly motivating.

Graduate student

Widgets on the home screen mean I plan without opening anything. Beautiful and fast.

Freelance designer

FAQ

Questions people ask

Is Nestly free?

Yes. The free plan covers tasks, lists and three habits on one device. Nestly Plus adds sync, Focus sessions, widgets and unlimited habits.

Which devices does it run on?

Phones and tablets on both major mobile platforms, plus a web app for your laptop. Your data syncs between all of them on Nestly Plus.

Can I import from another app?

Nestly imports plain text, CSV and calendar files. Paste a list and every line becomes a task.

Where is my data stored?

On your device first, and encrypted in our cloud if you turn on sync. We never sell data or show ads.

pages.title: About us
pages.content:
Nestly is made by a team of nine in a small studio by the river. We started it because every planner we tried wanted us to plan more, and we wanted to plan less.

What we promise

  • No ads, ever.
  • No selling or sharing of your data.
  • Your data stays on your device unless you turn on sync.
  • A free plan that is genuinely useful.

We are funded by Nestly Plus subscribers and nobody else, which keeps our incentives simple.

posts.title: Nestly 3.0: Focus sessions, a new Today view and widgets everywhere
posts.excerpt: Our biggest update yet: a rebuilt Today view, Focus sessions with history, and widgets for the home and lock screens.
posts.content:
Version 3

Nestly 3.0 is rolling out now. It is the update we have been working on all year, shaped by more than four thousand replies to our spring survey.

What’s new

  • Today, rebuilt. Swipe to pick tasks for today from your inbox in seconds.
  • Focus sessions. A calm timer with a history of what you finished.
  • Widgets. Today, Focus and Habits on your home and lock screens.
  • New themes. Six colour themes and four app icons.

Fixed

  • Reminders no longer fire twice after a time-zone change.
  • Habits marked on a tablet appear on the phone immediately.
  • VoiceOver reads task due dates in full.

Update from your app store. Your lists, habits and settings carry over automatically.

posts.title: Version 2.9: faster sync and a calmer notification centre
posts.excerpt: Sync is now up to five times faster, and notifications are grouped so your phone buzzes less.
posts.content:
Version 2.9

A smaller release with two improvements you will feel every day.

Improvements

  • Sync rewritten on a new protocol: changes arrive in under a second.
  • Notifications grouped by list, with a single morning summary option.
  • Search finds tasks by note text as well as title.

Fixes

  • Completed recurring tasks no longer reappear for a moment.
  • Dark mode colours corrected on older tablets.

Thank you to the beta group for a month of very detailed bug reports.

posts.title: Home screen widgets: how we designed them
posts.excerpt: Widgets are tiny, glanceable and updated rarely. Designing for those limits made our main app better too.
posts.content:
A widget gets a second of attention and refreshes on the system’s schedule, not ours. That forced us to decide what matters most about each screen.

Three rules we kept

  1. One question per widget: What’s next? How long is left? Did I do it today?
  2. No numbers without context: “3 left” beats “3”.
  3. Every tap goes somewhere specific, never just to the app’s home.

The Today widget turned out to be the clearest version of the Today view, so we brought its layout back into the app in 3.0.

Widgets are part of Nestly Plus. Add them from your home screen’s edit mode, then pick Today, Focus or Habits in three sizes.

posts.title: Building a habit that sticks: what our data says
posts.excerpt: Anonymous, aggregated data from habit tracking points to three simple things that help habits last past the first month.
posts.content:
We looked at anonymous, aggregated habit data from people who opted in to share it. Three patterns stood out among habits still going after sixty days.

What lasting habits have in common

  • They are small. “Read one page” outlasts “read for an hour” by a wide margin.
  • They have a time. Habits tied to a moment in the day last longer.
  • They survive a miss. People who came back after a missed day were the most consistent later.

Missing once is an accident. Missing twice is the start of a new habit.

A line from our onboarding screen

That last finding is why Nestly shows a week of dots instead of a streak counter. A broken streak feels like failure; a week with five dots feels like progress.

posts.title: Sync across phone, tablet and laptop without thinking about it
posts.excerpt: How Nestly keeps your devices in step, what happens offline, and three settings worth checking.
posts.content:
Sync is the feature you should never notice. Here is what happens behind the scenes, and the few settings that are worth a look.

Offline first

Every change is saved on your device immediately and sent when a connection is available. If two devices edit the same task, the most recent change to each field wins, so nothing is lost.

Three settings to check

  1. Background refresh on, so widgets stay current.
  2. Notifications on one device only, if you prefer a quiet tablet.
  3. The web app signed in with the same account.

Sync is part of Nestly Plus and is end-to-end encrypted for notes and task titles.

posts.title: Five ways to plan a week in ten minutes
posts.excerpt: A short Sunday ritual that makes Monday easier, using nothing but the week view and a cup of tea.
posts.content:
Weekly planning does not need a framework. Ten minutes with the week view on a Sunday evening is enough for most people.

The ritual

  1. Empty your inbox into lists, without deciding anything yet.
  2. Put fixed commitments on their days first.
  3. Give each day one important task, no more.
  4. Leave Friday afternoon empty on purpose.
  5. Pick tomorrow’s Today list and close the app.

If a day looks overloaded, Nestly tints it gently. Move something before the day arrives rather than during it.

After a few weeks the ritual takes less than ten minutes, and Monday mornings start with a plan instead of a pile.

posts.title: Why Focus sessions have no streaks
posts.excerpt: We prototyped streaks, badges and leaderboards for Focus. Then we removed all of them. Here is why.
posts.content:
Early versions of Focus sessions had streaks, badges and a weekly leaderboard among friends. Testers used it more in the first week and much less by the third.

What we saw

  • Streaks turned a missed day into a reason to quit.
  • Badges rewarded long sessions, not finished work.
  • Leaderboards made people anxious rather than focused.

The version we shipped asks one question when the timer ends: what did you finish? The history shows completed work, not minutes.

We wanted Focus to feel like closing a door, not like entering a competition.

Nestly design team
